why: ayodhya.300.cau3 'कृपा अनुग्रहु अंगु अघाई। कीन्हि कृपानिधि सब अधिकाई' — what is अंगु? (a) 'अंग-अंगमें, पूरी तरह' (every part, fully): Gita Press reads it so ('साङ्गोपाङ्ग'), and our meaning already says 'अंग-अंगमें'. (b) 'अंगीकार, अपनाना' (taking me as his own): the -उ ending makes अंगु a noun like अनुग्रहु beside it, so the line reads as a list 'kindness, favour, acceptance — to the full'; Platts gives अंग as 'body, limb; part, portion, share' and अंगीकार separately as 'acceptance', with no 'fully' sense for अंग. Platts and MW do not decide it. I would choose (b) for the grammar (three nouns, then अघाई 'to the full'); it means changing the entry to 'अंगीकार (अपनाना)' / 'acceptance' and our meaning's 'अंग-अंगमें' to 'अपनाया'. Keeping (a) means the entry becomes 'अंग-अंगमें, पूरी तरह' / 'in every part, fully'. Which?

ayodhya.311.cau3 'कुस कंटक काँकरीं कुराईं' (the earth hid the kuśa, thorns, pebbles and ___ from Bharata's path): is कुराईं 'ढेले' (clods; our entry and our meaning) or 'दरारें' (cracks, ruts; Gita Press)? Platts has no कुराई in either sense (its कुराई is 'stocks for the feet'); MW/Apte do not apply; the line fits both (hard, rough things on a path). Nothing I have settles it. I would keep 'ढेले' (clods), since it sits in a list of loose things lying on the path (kuśa, thorns, pebbles) that the earth 'hid'; if you have a reading of it in a dictionary or commentary (Śabdasāgar, McGregor), please say which.

lanka.67.cau3 'रन मद मत्त निसाचर दर्पा। बिस्व ग्रसिहि जनु एहि बिधि अर्पा': is दर्पा (a) a verb, 'was swollen with pride' (Gita Press: 'गर्वित हुआ'; it rhymes with अर्पा, 'offered', a verb, and gives the line its predicate), or (b) a noun, 'pride' (Platts: दर्पा = दर्प, pride, arrogance; Platts has no verb दर्पना), reading 'the rākṣasa's pride (was such) as if Fate had offered him the world to swallow'? The entry's adjective 'घमंड से भरा' has no support either way. I would choose (a): entry hi 'घमंडमें भर गया', en 'swelled with pride', r 'दर्प', g 'भूतकाल'; our meaning ('ऐसे गर्वमें भरा था') already fits it. Which?

bal.333.cau3 'पठईं जनक अनेक सुसारा' (Janaka sent many ___ to the barāt's halts): is सुसारा (a) 'सुन्दर शय्याएँ' (fine beds; Gita Press), (b) 'सुख-सुविधाकी वस्तुएँ' (comforts, things for the guests' ease; Platts: सुसार = substance, property; convenience, accommodation), or (c) our entry's 'अच्छी वस्तुएँ / fine provisions' (food — but the food was the line before, and Platts' only food-sense is सुसार 'a cook')? I would choose (b): it is Platts' sense and covers beds without guessing; entry hi 'सुख-सुविधाकी वस्तुएँ', en 'comforts, furnishings', r 'सुसार'. If you know the word as 'bed' (Gita Press's reading; the feminine पठईं fits शय्या), choose (a).

Śrī Rudram, Chamakam 5.6 'श्यामञ्च मे लोहञ्च मे' (just after 5.4 'हिरण्यञ्च मेऽयश्च मे', gold and अयः). Which metals are श्याम and लोह? (a) As now: अयः iron, श्याम copper, लोह bronze. That gives three different metals, and it looks like a commentator's reading (Sāyaṇa / Mahīdhara), but no copy of the commentary is at hand to confirm it. (b) Monier-Williams: लोह is 'red metal, copper', citing the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, whose Chamakam has the same list, and श्याम means only 'dark'. On that reading श्याम is the dark metal, iron, लोह is copper, and अयः becomes 'metal' in general (MW: अयस् 'iron, metal'). Calling copper 'the dark metal', as the entry now does, fits neither source. I would choose (b) unless an online Chamakam meaning you trust that follows Sāyaṇa gives copper and bronze; then keep (a) and drop '(the dark metal)'.

Same question as श्यामञ्च (Chamakam 5.6): is लोह bronze (now) or copper? Monier-Williams gives 'red metal, copper' for this list in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā. The present bronze looks like a commentator's reading that we cannot confirm here. Decide together with श्यामञ्च: (b) gives श्याम = iron, लोह = copper (ताँबा), अयः = metal; (a) keeps श्याम = copper, लोह = bronze. I would choose (b).
a11.salok 'ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ': Darpan glosses ਕਰਣ as ਜਗਤ/ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ (creation), ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ = the cause of creation; entry has 'करनेवाला/doer' (popular reading). Check Darpan before changing
a14.p3 'ਸੇ ਧਨਵੰਤ ਗਨੀ ਸੰਸਾਰ': may be Persian ਗਨੀ (ghani, rich) rather than 'counted' (Sant Singh: 'wealthy and prosperous'); site Hindi has 'गिने जाते हैं'. Possibly needs a second sense
a21.p7 'ਪਾਪੁ ਪੁੰਨੁ ਤਹ ਭਈ ਕਹਾਵਤ': feminine ਭਈ suggests ਕਹਾਵਤ is a fem. noun (talk/mention) rather than a present participle; g may be wrong
root 'ਉਪਾਰਜਣਾ' looks coined; Darpan relates ਉਪਰਜਾ to Skt उपार्जन (produced); a Sanskrit root (उप+अर्ज्) may be better

a13.p7 'ਸੰਤ ਕੈ ਦੋਖਿ ਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਟੈ ਕੋਇ': both site translations say 'is satisfied', but the form may derive from Skt तिष्ठ- (stands, holds firm) as some teekas gloss it; no root given. Verify against Darpan
root ਪਰਾਨਣਾ is not a standard dictionary verb; sense 'recognizes, considers' (Darpan: ਪਛਾਣਦਾ ਹੈ) is right but the root needs checking
ਉਨ ਜਨ ਚਰਨ ਪਰਾਤਾ: may be 'has fallen (at the feet)' (past) rather than present 'पड़ता है'
Darpan may read ਪਾਸਾਰੀ as 'the one who spreads the show' rather than noun 'display'
root ਪੁੱਜਣਾ is doubtful: ਪੁਨੀ (ਇਛ ਪੁਨੀ 'wish fulfilled') is usually derived from पूर्ण (ਪੁੰਨਾ/ਪੁੰਨੀ = completed), not ਪੁੱਜਣਾ 'to reach'
ਪ੍ਰਭ ਦਰਸ ਪਿਆਸਾ may be adjective 'thirsty (for)' rather than noun 'thirst'; g says स्त्री॰ though form is -ਾ
ਹਉਮੈ ਬਿਖੁ ਫੈਲੁ: Darpan/Mahan Kosh may read ਫੈਲੁ as noun 'spread, ostentation' (or Persian fe'l 'deed'); entry gives adjective 'फैला हुआ' / 'all-consuming'
ਏਕ ਬਸਤੁ ਕਾਰਨਿ ਬਿਖੋਟਿ ਗਵਾਵੈ: hi 'विश्वास (खोकर)' mixes the verb ਗਵਾਵੈ into the gloss; Darpan reads ਬਿਖੋਟਿ roughly as 'by breach of faith / dishonesty'; needs a teeka check
root ਡੁੱਬਣਾ is the modern synonym; the Gurbani verb is ਬੂਡਣਾ/ਬੂਡਨਾ (Hindi बूड़ना); keep the glossary convention in mind before changing
ਜਨ ਕੈ ਬਿਰਤਿ ਬਿਬੇਕੈ: hi 'विवेककी, विवेकपूर्ण' (genitive/adjective) vs g संज्ञा; case of -ੈ here needs a teeka check
ਬੋਲਹਿ ਹਰਿ ਮੁਖੀ: whether ਮੁਖੀ = 'chief, Supreme' (as entry) or 'with the mouth / turned towards' needs a teeka check
root ਲਹਿਣਾ (modern 'to come down/off') vs Gurbani ਲਹਣਾ 'to obtain' (< लभ्): same spelling in the glossary would mislead; consider a distinct root
root ਲਹਿਣਾ: the 'obtain' verb is Gurbani ਲਹਣਾ (< लभ्), distinct from modern ਲਹਿਣਾ 'come down'
root ਲਹਿਣਾ: the 'obtain/find' verb is Gurbani ਲਹਣਾ (< लभ्), distinct from modern ਲਹਿਣਾ 'come down'
ਜਿਸੁ ਧਨ ਤੇ ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਵਰਸਾਵੈ: hi mixes 'लाभ उठाता है' with 'बरसाता है' (rains); Darpan sense is 'is blessed/benefits'; 'बरसाता' likely wrong
ਜੈਸੇ ਸੂਰੁ ਸਰਬ ਕਉ ਸੋਖ: g 'संज्ञा' / hi 'सोखना' (infinitive) — here it functions verbally ('dries up / warms all'); grammar label needs a teeka check

सहरोसा (bal.208.cau2 सर्बस देउँ आजु सहरोसा, Daśaratha offering Viśvāmitra everything; aranya.43.cau2 सुनु मुनि तोहि कहउँ सहरोसा, Rāma to Nārada). Platts gives the word itself: सहरोसा = सह+रोष, 'angry, wrathful' (= सक्रोध). Gita Press reads 'हर्षके साथ / gladly' in both places, which is what our entry has (with a wrong root 'सहर्ष'). Anger fits neither line literally; our aranya meaning takes the middle 'with vehemence, emphatically' (रोष as fervour). Choose: (a) 'ज़ोर देकर, आवेशसे / with fervour, emphatically', root सह+रोष, as Platts' etymology and our meaning (my choice: it keeps the dictionary's word and fits both lines: 'I give all today, wholeheartedly'; 'I tell you emphatically'); or (b) keep 'सहर्ष / gladly' as Gita Press. Either way the root should be सह + रोष, not सहर्ष.
